title: Verification of Incomplete Graph Unlearning through Adversarial Perturbations

problem.claim: A dishonest model provider may perform incomplete edge unlearning by removing only a subset of requested edges from a trained graph neural network.

gap.claim: The paper addresses the need to verify whether requested graph edge unlearning was completed.

contributions.claim: PANDA is a probabilistic framework for verifying graph unlearning and detecting incomplete edge unlearning.
The paper provides an algorithm to identify token nodes and generate associated challenge edges.
The paper quantifies the verification probabilities achieved by PANDA.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive empirical studies reportedly show that PANDA is efficient and effective for detecting incomplete edge unlearning across various graph neural network models and unlearning algorithms.
The authors report that PANDA has strong robustness against state-of-the-art detection methods for graph adversarial perturbations.
The authors state that their code and datasets are available online.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph unlearning allows data owners to remove specific data from trained graph neural networks.
A dishonest provider may cheat by incompletely removing requested edges.
PANDA injects challenge edges connected to token nodes and uses prediction changes after requested removal to assess incomplete unlearning.
The method includes an algorithm for constructing token nodes and challenge edges and quantifies verification probabilities.
Empirical studies report effectiveness, efficiency, and robustness across models, unlearning algorithms, and adversarial-perturbation detection methods.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the verification probability guarantees.
The abstract does not report quantitative empirical results.
The abstract does not describe the experimental datasets, models, or unlearning algorithms in detail.
